title: Bridge Transport Record
description: DC-003-I029.1, extended by DC-003-I029.3 — one immutable transport event: one Engineering Work Order moved out, one Engineering Delivery Report moved in, or (as of I029.3) one Engineering Strategy Review moved out. Transport is intentionally dumb — this record proves a move happened and how, never why. `transport_type` is deliberately free-form (not a closed enum) since Bridge Transport must remain provider-neutral and support a future real transport provider without a schema change (mirrors publisher-result.schema.json's own free-form `provider` field for the same reason) — only 'mock' is ever produced. `object_type`/`object_id`/`direction` are tied together, direction always relative to the Strategy Office: an Engineering Work Order only ever travels outgoing (Strategy Office -> Delivery Office); an Engineering Delivery Report only ever travels incoming (Delivery Office -> Strategy Office); an Engineering Strategy Review only ever travels outgoing (Strategy Office -> Delivery Office or the CEO escalation path) — matching each milestone's own architecture diagram, not an invented rule. This I029.3 addition is purely additive — no existing field, enum value, or behaviour for engineering_work_order/engineering_delivery_report changed.

transport_type.description: The transport mechanism used — 'mock' is the only value this milestone ever produces. Free-form so a future real provider (e.g. an MCP/n8n/API bridge) needs no schema change.

status.description: pending: reserved for a future asynchronous transport provider — the mock transport is synchronous and never leaves a record pending. delivered: the move succeeded. rejected: the move failed (duplicate, corrupted payload, or transport failure) — rejected records are still kept, as transport history.

checksum.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the transported object's own canonical JSON — used for duplicate/corruption detection, never a substitute for schema validation.
